articles.title: 4 WWE stars who disrespected Nikki Bella with John Cena relationship remarks
articles.summary: WWE News: A major chapter in WWE Hall of Famer Nikki Bella's life was her relationship with John Cena. The duo was together for a long time. However, they parte.
articles.body: A major chapter in WWE Hall of Famer Nikki Bella's life was her relationship with John Cena. The duo was together for a long time. However, they parted ways in 2018 because their beliefs and life goals didn't align. Over the years, multiple superstars have taken huge jabs at Bella in that context. However, these four WWE stars really went over the line:4. AJ LeeAJ Lee was the reigning WWE Divas Champion in 2014 when the Bella Twins were getting all the hype due to their high-profile relationships and reality TV series, Total Divas. During a promo segment on RAW, Lee mocked both Nikki Bella and her sister by taking a jab regarding their boyfriends, John Cena and Daniel Bryan, respectively. She said, “It’s about time somebody breaks it to the Bellas, talent is not s*xually transmitted.”3. Ronda RouseyRonda Rousey had been on top of the women’s division for a year in WWE in 2018. The Bella Twins returned and, after a brief alliance, turned their back on the Rowdy One. During a heated promo exchange, Nikki said that she has broken more barriers and doors than Rousey. This led Rousey to retaliate and say: “The only door you knocked down was a door to John Cena’s bedroom. He eventually threw you out of that door.”2. Becky LynchBecky Lynch and Nikki Bella engaged in a rivalry following The Fearless One’s WWE comeback in 2025. A memorable in-ring segment saw both superstars trade heated words. The Man boasted that she and her husband, Seth Rollins, were WWE's top wrestling couple. Right then, Lynch said that at one point it was Nikki Bella and John Cena without mentioning his name. Moreover, Lynch ended the rant by saying that Bella could not see him anymore. Lynch said, “You can’t see him anymore.”1. Paige Nikki Bella began a feud with Paige after betraying her after their six-woman tag team matches at SummerSlam 2026. The two women met in a backstage segment on SmackDown ahead of their battle in Mexico City a week later. Paige took the opportunity to make a huge John Cena remark at her, saying, “I built my career on Hustle, Loyalty, and Respect, while you just slept with it.”Also read: WWE has no plans for wrestling star Cody Rhodes' heel turn yet, despite darker character teaseGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton’s US Open night takes a shocking turn as Martina Navratilova reacts to 3:33 a.m. finish
articles.summary: International Sports News: Martina Navratilova has criticized the US Open schedule after Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton’s quarterfinal started around 11 p.m. and finished at 3:3.
articles.body: Martina Navratilova has criticized the US Open schedule after Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton’s quarterfinal started around 11 p.m. and finished at 3:33 a.m. on Tuesday night. The match became the latest finish in US Open history, according to the official US Open website. Navratilova reacted to the late start on X, saying the tournament needs to make changes because such timings are not normal for players.Martina Navratilova calls Carlos Alcaraz-Ben Shelton’s late US Open start “not OK”Martina Navratilova has criticized the US Open schedule after Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton were forced to begin their quarterfinal after 11 p.m. on Tuesday night. The match then went deep into the early morning, finishing at 3:33 a.m. local time. The official US Open website confirmed that it was the latest finish in tournament history. Navratilova reacted on X while the scheduling delay was becoming clear.“Something has got to give… this is not ok and it is not normal … no other sport might start at 11 AM or 11 PM. In the same event…” Navratilova wrote on X.The delay came after a long day on Arthur Ashe Stadium. The schedule began at 11:30 a.m. with Aryna Sabalenka facing Linda Noskova. Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen followed, and their match lasted four hours and 38 minutes. That pushed the later matches well behind their planned times.Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro then played the first match of the night session. Their contest also went beyond two hours, which meant Alcaraz and Shelton did not get onto court until after 11 p.m. By then, the two players were facing a very different challenge from the one they would have faced with an earlier start.Navratilova’s complaint was aimed at the scheduling rather than either player. Her point was that the same event can begin matches in the morning and still have players starting another match around 11 p.m. The former world No. 1 has also spoken out about late-night tennis during this year’s tournament.Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton finish latest US Open match at 3:33 a.m.Once the match finally started, neither Carlos Alcaraz nor Ben Shelton was able to finish the contest quickly. The quarterfinal lasted four hours and 28 minutes and went to a deciding-set tiebreak before Shelton pulled off one of the biggest wins of his career.The official US Open website reported that the No. 8 seed beat defending champion Alcaraz 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6(7). Shelton ended the match with a 146-mph ace at 3:33 a.m., setting the tournament’s latest finishing time.The win also gave Shelton his first victory over a player ranked inside the world’s top three. He will now face fellow American Frances Tiafoe in Friday’s semifinal. Alcaraz, meanwhile, saw his US Open title defense come to an end after he had won his previous 18 Grand Slam matches.The late finish was especially striking because the match itself was so demanding. Shelton had to stay focused through five sets after waiting until late at night to begin, while Alcaraz also had to deal with the physical demands of a match that ended in the early hours of the morning.For Navratilova, that was the larger issue. Her message pointed to a scheduling system that can leave players waiting for hours before being asked to play a major match, with the final point sometimes coming close to sunrise.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lewis Hall: Man United receive glimmer of hope in pursuit of Newcastle ace
articles.summary: 1Manchester United’s pursuit of Newcastle United left-back Lewis Hall ended in disappointment this summer. The Red Devils were looking for a long-term replac...
articles.body:
Manchester United's pursuit of Newcastle United left-back Lewis Hall ended in disappointment this summer. The Red Devils were looking for a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw and had identified the 21 year old as a priority target for the job.

Fast, technically gifted and blessed with an excellent passing range, Hall is a modern full-back who blends attacking desire with defensive discipline. His attributes make him a fantastic successor for Shaw at the Theatre of Dreams.

The 31 year old has entered the final year of his contract with United and the Red Devils wanted Hall to take his place. While the move failed to materialise, the English giants are expected to return for the player next summer.

However, a recent report relayed by The Peoples Person suggests that the young full-back is all set to sign a new deal at St. James' Park, raising doubts about a move to Old Trafford. While that has added to United's frustrations, a fresh update has now emerged from journalist Ben Jacobs that could be a shot in the arm for fans.

Speaking to talkSPORT , Jacobs said Hall is now tied to Newcastle United until 2031. He stated: "It's a five-year contract that adds two years to the existing deal. So it keeps Hall at the club until 2031. There were always these two extremes at play. Either Manchester United would make an approach, would have to overpay, and Hall would have been somewhat open to that move."

"Or he stays and under the new manager, Matthias Jaissle, is invested in the project, and then he signs a new deal. But it was never just going to continue with Hall staying and not being offered improved terms."

Jacobs insisted that Hall was not unsettled at St. James' Park, which has helped in the renewal process. He added: "Newcastle have been able to keep Hall because he was never unhappy with Newcastle the club, only unhappy with how last season ended, where he was in and out of the side."

"He lost his England place. Dan Burn , his Newcastle teammate, got picked in his place. All of that led Hall to, in the early part of the summer, at least put the brakes on signing because the nuts and bolts of this deal were in place in February or March."

"Then Eddie Howe leaves, Matthias Jaissle comes in. He's had a very positive effect on all players, including Lewis Hall. And Jaissle has told Hall he is integral, he is the number one left-back. Then from there, there was no hesitation in getting this deal over the line."

Jacobs went on to cite the example of Morgan Rogers to explain why a move cannot be entirely ruled out next summer. The English forward signed a new contract with Aston Villa in 2025, and joined Chelsea in a blockbuster transfer this summer.

Referring to that saga, Jacobs added: "Of course, we have to say with Morgan Rogers, he extended late last year. He still left the following summer."

"So I don't think we can say categorically, depending on how the season goes, that Hall is unavailable in the summer 2027 market. But it's a really positive sign for Newcastle. If everything now goes according to plan, then Hall will remain invested in this project."

Prising Hall away from Newcastle United has just become harder following his decision to sign a new deal. While United are likely to keep him under close watch, they could also consider alternative targets like Adrien Truffert .

The Peoples Person Reliability Assessment Overall credibility: 8/10 Why?

✅ Ben Jacobs is a well-respected journalist.✅ The report ties in with a recent one saying Newcastle will still have to sell next summer.⚠️ It is pure speculation on Jacobs' part at the moment.

articles.title: Pair of NFL experts do not have Bengals making the playoffs
articles.summary: An ESPN writer and an NFL.com reporter have the Bengals on the outside of the playoffs again this year.
articles.body:
Kyle Brandt revealed his selections to make the AFC playoffs on Good Morning Football Tuesday morning. The Cincinnati Bengals were not among the teams he chose to make it to the playoffs.

After missing the playoffs for three straight seasons, it seems the Bengals still have a lot to prove when it comes to the media. Brandt selected the Baltimore Ravens to win the AFC North this season. A pick that going into this season is at least understandable.

The Ravens have won the AFC North two out of the last three seasons. The rushing attack returns Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson . For a preseason prediction, there is at least nothing egregious about this one, even if it isn't the selection I would have personally made.

The more interesting selection came with his final wild card team. Brandt chose the Tennessee Titans to nab the final wild card spot for the AFC.

Robert Salah takes over as the head coach for the Titans, with Cam Ward entering his second season as the starting quarterback. While I do expect that defense to keep them competitive in a lot of games, I just don't think they have the offensive firepower to be a playoff team this year.

If we see the Titans make the playoffs over the Bengals something has gone seriously wrong. The Bengals added Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen , Boye Mafe , Cashius Howell, and Bryan Cook as key contributors to a revamped defense. The entire starting offensive line returns for the first time in the Joe Burrow era. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best receiver tandem in the entire NFL.

Elsewhere, ESPN's Bill Barnwell's 2026 season predictions also do not have the Bengals making it back to the postseason. Barnwell has the Chiefs , Patriots , Ravens, and Texans winning their respective AFC divisions, while the Bills, Broncos , and Steelers of all teams get the Wild Card spots. He also has the Chiefs beating the Eagles to win the Super Bowl.

There are a lot of reasons to be optimistic as Bengals fans heading into the first game of the season on Sunday. It appears they will have to convince a lot of the media as the season goes.

Personally, I don't mind them being underdogs in the eyes of the talking heads around the league. The time is now, go out and show the world exactly who you are. It is time to make a run at winning the whole thing this season.

articles.title: World 100 Driver Rankings: Seeding The Entire 2026 Field
articles.summary: Ranking all 105 drivers in the 2026 World 100 field, from Eldora Speedway favorites Bobby Pierce and Jonathan Davenport to long-shot contenders.
articles.body:
The World 100 annually brings together Dirt Late Model racing's best to Eldora Speedway. If every driver arrived in Rossburg, Ohio, with a seed beside their name, how would the field stack up?

Ahead of Sept. 10-12's World 100, we're ranking every expected entrant based on current form, Eldora performance, event history and the subjective factors separating contenders from the rest.

These aren't cut-and-dried predictions of where each driver will finish, nor simply a ranking of the sport's best drivers. The question is more specific: Who enters World 100 weekend with the strongest case to outperform everyone seeded behind him at one of the sport's most demanding venues?

Each ranking includes the driver's hometown and a personalized outlook for World weekend along with previous credentials. From Eldora favorites to drivers chasing Saturday's feature, here's how we seed the 2026 World 100 field (seeding best-known entries as of Tuesday night):

Background: Capturing four of the last six Eldora crown jewels, including June's Dream, Pierce has supplanted Jonathan Davenport as the new favorite at the Big E. He did look vincible in last year's World 100, unable to fully overcome the invert while rallying from 27th to ninth. Amid another monstrous 27-win campaign, he'll try to become the first driver to capture five Eldora crown jewels in a seven-race span.

2. Jonathan Davenport (49), Blairsville, Ga.

Best World 100 finish: 1st (2015, '17, '19, '21, '22)

Background: Five-time World 100 winner remains gold standard at Eldora, finishing seventh or better in seven consecutive editions. He enters with 14 victories, including a dominant $50,000 triumph at half-mile Port Royal two weeks ago, but has gone winless in the last three Eldora crown jewels — and hasn't gone four straight without winning since the 2015 Dream. Another triumph would tie Billy Moyer for most World 100 victories and Scott Bloomquist for most overall Eldora crown jewels at 12.

3. Brandon Sheppard (1), New Berlin, Ill.

Background: The 17-time winner and Prairie Dirt Classic winner appeared capable of winning June's Dream before a right-front tire failure knocked him from second. He enters World week amid a season-long 14-race winless streak, however, and the World remains the glaring omission from his résumé, with sixth his best finish in 12 A-main starts. Still, his crown-jewel strength this season keeps him firmly in the top three.

4. Ricky Thornton Jr. (20RT), Chandler, Ariz.

Background: Thornton might not have cracked the top 10 a month ago, but he's peaking at the right time, since debuting a new car at the Topless 100. He's since produced his first three-race streak of top-two finishes since April 2025, highlighted by a dominant victory at half-mile Port Royal two weeks ago and 23 of 25 laps led in Sunday's Baltes Classic before a late slip-up. The defending World winner is also a perfect 7-for-7 in A-main attempts since his 2019 debut.

5. Dale McDowell (17M), Chickamauga, Ga.

Background: Perhaps nobody has been more dependable in the World than McDowell, whose 12 consecutive top-eight finishes include three straight podiums. He has gained 106 positions during that remarkable stretch, relentlessly contending regardless of where he starts. Twenty-one years after his breakthrough victory, the 60-year-old remains a legitimate threat to become the event's oldest winner.

Background: Emerging as one of Eldora's most reliable contenders, Hoffman's recorded two podiums and three top-fives in the track's last four 100-lap crown jewels. His third-place finish in last year's World was his best in six A-main starts, continue to fuel his Eldora-biggie-winning potential. Sunday's Baltes Classic victory snapped a three-month winless drought and supplied a timely boost entering World week.

7. Hudson O'Neal (71), Martinsville, Ind.

Background: The 16-time winner this year leads the nation with 45 podiums and 76 top-10 finishes, giving him an undeniable résumé. The 2023 World winner has nonetheless gone winless with his SSI Motorsports team since mid-May, a lengthy drought that doesn't mix well with recent World results of 11th and 25th since his 2023 triumph.

Background: Rolling into World week hungry to redeem a likely Dream podium lost to a wheel issue, Erb has three victories in his last six starts, including a win at half-mile Southern Iowa Speedway and a sweep of Portsmouth's $25,000 weekend. He followed that surge with a fifth-place finish in Sunday's Baltes Classic. After charging from 16th to fourth in last year's World, Erb possesses the dangerous combination of proven Eldora speed and timely momentum.

Background: Madden's elusive Eldora crown jewel remains one of Dirt Late Model racing's great unfinished stories after runner-up finishes in three Dreams, the Eldora Million and Dirt Track World Championship. After calling June's Dream DNQ "a total disaster," Madden returns encouraged by consecutive fourth-place finishes at half-mile Port Royal. A breakthrough would certainly carry shades of Dale Earnhardt's cathartic 1998 Daytona 500 victory.

Background: The reigning Lucas Oil Late Model Dirt Series champ enters World week refreshed after Sunday's Hillbilly 100 victory snapped a 21-race winless drought. The breakthrough added another 100-lap triumph to a seven-win season that also includes the Firecracker 100. His World résumé remains surprisingly modest, however, with a single top-five and three top-10s in 10 A-main starts.

Background: The 2021 World winner has eight victories across six tours, but none against a full field since April 15 at Volunteer Speedway; his latest came in an August North-South 100 prelim. He slipped from ninth to 13th in June's Dream after running third in last year's World before pitting on lap 37 and retiring on lap 70. He's still among contenders, qualifying for six straight World A-mains.

Background: Blair has a strong grasp of the Dream, improving from 10th to seventh to second in three appearances while gaining 22 positions overall. His fifth-place finish in the 2024 Dirt Track World Championship and recent 100-lap victory at Lernerville further validate his long-distance strength. Now he must solve the World, where he has qualified only once in three attempts and finished 27th last year.

Background: The complexion of Marlar's season shifted dramatically after he switched to a Rocket XR2 following his Dream DNQ, producing six wins, 10 podiums and 11 top-10s in 22 starts since. He has qualified for eight of the last 10 Worlds, highlighted by a runner-up finish in 2021, but placed 11th in last year's consolation. Few drivers are riding higher into World week.

Background: Like Marlar, the North-South 100 winner has upped his game since debuting a new Rocket XR2, collecting four wins and six podiums across his last 11 starts. Three consecutive podiums at Portsmouth and Eldora over the weekend eased concerns raised by non-factor finishes of 10th and 17th at half-mile Port Royal two weeks ago. The 2025 Dream prelim winner has qualified for four consecutive Worlds, twice finishing a career-best 14th.

Background: The two-time Eldora major winner is the quintessential glass-half-full-or-half-empty contender. Both victories this season came in World of Outlaws events on half-miles at Selinsgrove and Bedford, and he finished second at half-mile Adams County two weeks ago. But he missed June's Dream by one position, while last year's 19th-place World finish ended a streak of six consecutive top-10s.

16. Ryan Gustin (19R), Marshalltown, Iowa

Background: Gustin might be ranked a bit low considering his last three World finishes of eighth, ninth and fifth, but it's difficult to justify placing him ahead of anyone above him.

17. Chris Ferguson (22), Mount Holly, N.C.

Background: Ferguson is among the few part-time operations capable of winning an Eldora prelim and contending in the 100-lapper, having charged from 26th to eighth in last year's World, finished ninth in June's Dream and qualified for six of the last seven Worlds.

Background: Winger's nine wins and charge from 19th to eighth in June's Dream point to his considerable upside, but he hasn't made a World A-main since 2021.

Background: With 11 victories and 43 top-10s in 56 starts on the season, the steady Feger believes he found an Eldora package in June's 15th-place Dream run and now seeks consecutive World A-mains for the first time since making three straight from 2012-14.

20. Daulton Wilson (58v), Fayetteville, N.C.

Background: The Viper-Big Frog Motorsports driver has qualified for seven consecutive Eldora crown jewels and finished 16th in June's Dream, making his consistency in Rossburg more meaningful than his one-win season.

Best World 100 finish: No starts in a single attempt.

Background: Some might think Ebert is ranked too high, but he's earning his keep following a 26th-to-11th charge in his Eldora crown jewel debut at June's Dream with an attrition-filled Topless 100 victory.

22. Ethan Dotson (74), Bakersfield, Calif.

Background: The ASD Motorsports driver owns national victories with the World of Outlaws and at the Wild West Shootout and is 2-for-2 in World A-main attempts, although both ended in DNFs.

23. Trey Mills (14jr), St. Augustine, Fla.

Best World 100 finish: No starts in a single attempt

Background: The 19-year-old is far more capable than his 23rd rank suggests, having led 89 combined laps in the Dream and Prairie Dirt Classic before sweeping Brownstown's John Gill Classic over Hudson O'Neal and Mike Marlar and finishing fourth in Sunday's Baltes Classic.

Background: The Robby Allen-led driver who came two spots shy of his first World A-main since 2021 has dominated regionally with 11 wins in 32 starts, but owns only one top-10 and a 15.1 average finish across 10 national races.

Background: The 21-year-old has two victories and five podiums in 14 starts with new car owner Jerry Foster, while qualifying for both of his Eldora crown jewel attempts — a career-best 18th in last year's World 100 debut and 24th in June's Dream.

26. Sam Seawright (16), Rainsville, Ala.

Background: Like Mills, the Coltman Farms Racing driver is far more capable than his ranking suggests, bringing four wins and his 10th-place finish at the Dream this June into his World debut.

Background: The 2022 Dirt Track World Championship winner's eighth-place 2024 World finish and three A-mains in four years separate him from similarly productive drivers.

Background: The former fourth-place finisher has made 11 World A-mains, but only one victory and two podiums this season temper his ranking as he attempts to qualify for four consecutive editions for the first time.

29. Tyler Carpenter (13), Parkersburg, W.Va.

Best World 100 finish: No starts in six attempts

Background: Popular West Virginia driver might have his best opportunity yet aboard Cody Sommer's DRT house car after agonizingly missing the last three World A-mains by one, three and one positions.

Background: Eight World A-mains and last year's consolation near-miss — one position behind Bobby Pierce — offset a winless, two-podium 2026 season.

31. Kyle Strickler (8), Mooresville, N.C.

Background: Scott Bloomquist's former mentee and cornerstone of Austin Kirkpatrick's chassis builds is one of 10 drivers to make six consecutive Worlds, but four straight event DNFs and only nine top-10s in 29 starts this season lower his ceiling.

Background: A Lucas Oil sweep of July's Diamond Nationals and a top-10 finish two weeks ago at half-mile Port Royal raise expectations for the World rookie.

33. Carson Ferguson (93), Lincolnton, N.C.

Background: Amid an uneven season featuring one $3,000 victory at Florence and a Dream DNQ by five positions, the Paylor Motorsports has reason for confidence qualifying for two consecutive World 100s.

Background: The 17-time World 100 A-main starter has missed the last two Dreams and Worlds but returns with momentum after winning twice in his last four starts.

Background: The five-time Lernerville champion remains an Eldora threat despite only two wins in 16 starts this season and returns looking to avenge missing last year's World A-main by three positions.

36. Dennis Erb Jr. (28), Carpentersville, Ill.

Background: The former Dream winner and 13-time World starter remains capable — he finished 11th last year — but a winless season and Dream DNQ temper his prospects.

37. Dustin Sorensen (19), Rochester, Minn.

Background: A recent Oskaloosa podium and a 2-for-2 record qualifying for the Dream suggest the third-year touring driver could make noise in his World debut.

Background: The Skyline Motorsports open-competition rookie has experienced equal parts promise and growing pains, but missing the Dream by one position in his Eldora crown jewel debut offers encouragement.

Best World 100 finish: No starts in two attempts

Background: Productive Southerner owns four wins and 13 podiums and was one position from transferring through his Dream heat before hitting the wall, making him a strong first-time qualifier candidate in his sixth Eldora crown jewel attempt.

Background: Eldora has tantalized Joiner, who's started on the pole of his World heat the last two years yet enters with five consecutive crown jewel DNQs, including missing June's Dream by three spots.

41. Tristan Chamberlain (20TC), Richmond, Ind.

Background: Sunday's Baltes Classic victory suggests the 18-year-old could end a streak of four consecutive Eldora crown jewel DNQs since making his first World A-main in 2023.

Background: Opie's 12 victories make him one of the season's most productive, but last year's World 100 and Dream trips yielded two consolation near-misses and a 2026 Dream withdrawal because of mechanical trouble.

43. Jason Jameson (12), Lawrenceburg, Ind.

Background: Twelve podiums and two victories in 32 regional starts are encouraging, though he missed June's Dream by two positions and has qualified for only one World in eight tries.

Best World 100 finish: No starts in single attempt

Background: Qualifying for June's Dream showcased the modified ace's potential, but only seven top-10s in 32 starts on the season temper his outlook.

Background: An unusually fragmented season across three chassis brands has yielded only three top-10s in 19 starts for the 19-time World A-main qualifier, though a season-best third Aug. 22 at Smoky Mountain offers hope.

Background: Eight podiums in 31 starts and a competitive 14th-place FloRacing Night in America finish at Eldora in June give the Juiceman legitimate sleeper appeal.

Background: The 18-year-old Michigan native enters with timely momentum from a North-South 100 podium and fifth-place Baltes finish, though his best Eldora crown jewel result is 10th in a Dream consolation.

48. Jadon Frame (81F), Winchester, Tenn.

Background: After missing last year's World transfer by four positions and finishing sixth in Sunday's Baltes Classic semifeature, the Riggs Motorsports driver has the goods to make his first A-main.

Background: Don't let two victories in only 14 starts fool you: the Team Christy Racing driver fell just three positions short of making the 2024 World in family-owned equipment.

50. Frank Heckenast Jr. (99jr), Frankfort, Ill.

Background: Three Summer Nationals wins and seven World A-mains barely earn him a top-50 spot, but he's missed every Eldora crown jewel since 2021 and averages 21.5 in his last four features there.

Background: Fell five positions short of transferring in his World 100 debut last year.

52. Michael Leach (09), Sun River, Mont.

Background: Typically brings a strong qualifying package and fell four spots short of a Dream transfer through a consolation race in June.

Background: Missed the World 100 A-main by three spots in a consolation race last year.

54. Jerry Bowersock (95J), Wapakoneta, Ohio

Background: Sixty-year-old has best shot in years to qualify for first World 100 A-main since 2013, coming fourth in Sunday's Eldora semi and already winning in new Rocket XR2.

55. Brenden Smith (17ss), Dade City, Fla.

Best World 100 finish: No starts in four attempts

76. Trevor Collins (11AC), Seaford, Del.

79. Jake Little (38J), Springfield, Ill.

Background: Sixth in points on MARS circuit with one top-five

80. Dillard Hatchett (59), Cornersville, Tenn.

Background: Seven top-fives in 2026 specials

Background: Twelfth in Sunday's Baltes Classic semifeature.

83. Duane Chamberlain (20C), Richmond, Ind.

Background: First World attempt since 2022; 19th in Sunday's Baltes Classic semi.

84. Rusty Ballenger (1G), Seymour, Tenn.

Background: Warrior house car driver fresh off $13,037 Limited victory at Wartburg

87. Mike Provenzano (M27), Marseilles, Ill.

Background: Son of 1992 World 100 starter John Provenzano

Background: Single MARS top-five in nine series feature starts

Background: Thirteenth in Sunday's Baltes Classic semi.

Background: Splits times between Supers, Crates

91. Tyler Thomason (7), Phenix City, Ala.

Background: Multitime East Alabama champ DNQ'd at Dream

92. Brandon Carpenter (51B), Coldwater, Miss.

Background: Seventh-place Summer Nationals finish at Red Hill

articles.title: Bengals’ Zac Taylor announces injury update for Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow gets major help for the NFL Week 1 opener as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins continue their recovery from injury.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals are preparing for their NFL season opener with Joe Burrow leading an offense that still revolves around Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . Cincinnati will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday at Paycor Stadium, beginning a season that comes with high expectations after another busy offseason. Burrow enters the season with his two primary receivers healthy enough to practice after both dealt with injuries late in the preseason. Chase hyperextended his knee during a joint practice, while Higgins has been dealing with a heel contusion. Both missed practice last week before returning Monday. Burrow and the Bengals need both receivers available as Chase and Higgins are two established targets who can win against man coverage.

Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on pace to play Sunday

Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins (5). Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images.

Head Coach Zac Taylor said Chase and Higgins are on pace to play against Tampa Bay . The Bengals coach had previously said both receivers would be limited during the week but expected them to be ready for the opener. Chase returned Monday after dealing with the knee issue, while Higgins also got back on the field. Their progress through the rest of the week will determine whether they enter Sunday without a game-status designation or carry one into the opener.

Joe Burrow gets his top weapons back for Week 1

The Bengals spent the offseason improving the roster around Burrow. Cincinnati added Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen to the defensive line while also continuing to build around its established offensive core. Burrow has also made clear that he remains committed to Cincinnati and believes the offseason changes have put the team in a better position entering 2026. Having Chase and Higgins available gives Burrow the best version of his passing attack to start the season. Cincinnati's offense has little room for error after a 6-11 season in 2025, and the team has made significant changes around its quarterback. For a Bengals team trying to return to the playoffs, that is exactly how the offense needs to begin.

articles.title: Blue Jays could compete with Dodgers for Cy Young-winning ace in free agency
articles.summary: The Blue Jays could get into another bidding war with the Dodgers this offseason.
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays and Los Angeles Dodgers have been linked to each other for the past few seasons, especially since they went head-to-head in their pursuit of Shohei Ohtani . He went to the Dodgers, and the Blue Jays missed out.

But they made the World Series and had the Dodgers down to their last gasp; a homer to send the game to extras resulted in a heartbreaking Game 7 loss. Then, over the offseason, the two competed for Kyle Tucker before he chose the Dodgers.

Looking ahead to the 2026-2027 free agency window, the Blue Jays and Dodgers could compete again. CBS Sports' Mike Axisa named the Blue Jays and Dodgers as landing spots for Cy Young free agent ace Tarik Skubal for what could be another bidding war.

Blue Jays and Dodgers could get into a bidding war for Tarik Skubal

"Skubal is the clear-cut, inarguable No. 1 free agent," Axisa writes. "Super early possible landing spots: Blue Jays, Dodgers."

The Blue Jays are a real possible destination for Skubal in free agency. Their ownership group isn't afraid to spend money, and someone like Skubal would be just the kind of player worth splurging on.

He's going to cost a fortune, most likely north of $300 million overall, and potentially even beyond $400 million. But while expensive, the Blue Jays are a logical landing spot.

Pairing him with Dylan Cease could give the Blue Jays the elite 1-2 punch that many elite teams look for in their starting rotation.

Skubal has a 2.84 ERA in a down season by his standards. Cease is a strong Cy Young candidate in the AL this season. Having both pitchers, alongside Trey Yesavage and Jose Soriano, would make for an elite rotation.

Adding Skubal in free agency will be tricky, as they're going to have to outbid the Dodgers. It won't be easy, but if there's any team that could do it, it would be the Blue Jays.

They've gone head-to-head in the free agent market for a lot of the top players over the years, and maybe this time, to land Skubal, they'll come away as the winners.

articles.title: Miami's Toney, Pitt's Heintschel, Duke's Sheppard give ACC national leaders in FBS headlining stats
articles.summary: Malachi Toney couldn't be stopped, running free through Stanford's defense and striking Heisman Trophy poses after catching touchdown passes for seventh-rank...
articles.body:
Malachi Toney couldn't be stopped, running free through Stanford's defense and striking Heisman Trophy poses after catching touchdown passes for seventh-ranked Miami .

A day later, Pittsburgh's Mason Heintschel set an Atlantic Coast Conference single-game record for TD throws. And Nate Sheppard had a tough-running edge that carried Duke all day.

The ACC hasn't had a good start in marquee matchups against other power-conference teams. But the league enters Week 2 with at least one highlight: that sophomore trio posted the top receiving, passing and rushing totals in the Bowl Subdivision ranks, offering hope that there's the kind of skill-position talent that could help the ACC recover from its early hole.

"Because of the movement of the players and the transactional nature of the sport, we've spread the talent thinner so everybody's more competitively balanced," ESPN and ACC Network analyst Tom Luginbill said. "Which means you're going to be in more one-possession games than you've probably ever been in before. ... If you (win) that and you have top performances, now you start shifting the narrative.

"And it draws eyeballs. People are going to say, 'Wait, who's this guy? I haven't seen him.'"

That's not necessary for Toney, who thrived as Miami reached last year's College Football Playoff championship game and was a preseason Associated Press first-team All-American . Heintschel and Sheppard lack that same spotlight yet opened with starring performances, too.

Sophomore trio put up big stats amid ACC's bumpy start

Each was more productive than counterparts anywhere in the country:

Toney had a school-record 234 yards receiving against the Cardinal and is the only FBS player to crack the 200-yard mark through two weekends. His 12 catches were tied for most in a game.

Heintschel threw for a national-best 453 yards in a win against Miami (Ohio) , joining ACC quarterbacks Kevin Jennings of SMU (430 against Florida State) and Darian Mensah of Miami (401 while peppering Toney with targets) as FBS' only passers yet to surpass the 400-yard mark. Heintschel's seven TD throws broke the ACC record of six, which had been reached 11 times.

Sheppard ran for a national-best 227 yards with two TDs in a win against Tulane . Sheppard's 35 carries are the most of any FBS player this year and one of only two FBS performances of at least 30 carries.

Those offered individual highlights as the ACC went 1-5 against the Big 12, Big Ten and Southeastern Conference. North Carolina's win against TCU in Ireland stands as the lone victory in matchups that included No. 8 LSU running Clemson out of Baton Rouge in a game between marquee brands.

Toney finds immediate connection with Mensah

The 5-foot-11, 193-pound Toney delivered 1,211 yards and 10 touchdowns as a freshman, then opened with a dominant performance.

On Miami's first offensive snap at Stanford, he took a short pass to the left and got loose for a 48-yard gain before snagging a 23-yard TD throw. He also had a 2-yard TD grab and went deep for a 47-yard TD in the third quarter.

Toney said afterward that he had gotten faster since last year, while Miami coach Mario Cristobal called Toney an "elite route-runner." That combination helped Mensah post his own fast start with five TD throws after a high-profile transfer from Duke .

"Honestly just makes my job extremely easy as a quarterback," Mensah told reporters Tuesday. "He's almost like another quarterback on the field, just the way that he understands defense."

Heintschel's Year 1 experience shows to start Year 2

Pittsburgh coach Pat Narduzzi went to Heintschel as his starter about a month into last season . Heintschel said in July he felt he had more freedom to work in coordinator Kade Bell's offense with that experience.

He certainly looked in control against the RedHawks while completing 31 of 41 passes (75.6%).

"Coach Bell and I talk about that a lot," Heintschel said. "Take what the defense is giving us. (It's about) just kind of being boring sometimes."

He's the first FBS quarterback since LSU's Joe Burrow in 2019 to throw for at least 450 yards and seven TDs without an interception. Each TD throw went to a different receiver.

"It's very impactful," sophomore running back Ja'Kyrian Turner said. "The defense doesn't know what to do. The threat of Mason is him spreading out the offense. He's got a lot of playmakers he can get the ball to, and plenty of ways to get the offense going."

Sheppard carries a heavy workload in Week 1

With Mensah's move south, it was clear that the reigning ACC champion Blue Devils would lean on Sheppard after he ran for 1,132 yards and 11 TDs last year. Duke did exactly that Saturday, with Sheppard carrying the ball 10 times during a 17-play season-opening drive.

Add three catches, and Sheppard had 38 touches on Duke's 77 offensive plays (49.4%). So managing workload and health will be important going forward.

"He took the bulk of the carries last year, especially the second half of the season," offensive coordinator Jonathan Brewer said Monday. "I don't think this is new to him. Maybe direct runs instead of moreso lighter boxes, RPO type of runs — that kind of stuff is probably a little bit different. He probably had more touches on checkdowns last year than he did in that first game for us.

AP Sports Writer Will Graves in Pittsburgh contributed to this report.

articles.title: With Keider Montero on baby watch, Tigers tentatively juggle rotation
articles.summary: AJ Hinch keeping eye on the career-high level workloads of young right-handers Keider Montero and Troy Melton.
articles.body:
DETROIT — You'd never know it. He continues to go about his business with a carefree smile on his face. But Keider Montero has a lot of his plate these days. His fiancé is pregnant and expected to deliver soon.

There was some trepidation, even, over whether he'd be able to make his start in the series finale against the Twins on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Which, even as rain delayed the start of the game, he was prepared to do.

His fiancé is in Venezuela with no visa. So, Montero's only contact with her has been through FaceTime. The separation has also stalled their wedding plans.

The expectation is Montero will take paternity leave soon. The Tigers have already tentatively juggled their rotation in anticipation of his absence. Manager AJ Hinch said that Framber Valdez will start the series opener against the Rockies on Friday and Jackson Jobe will start Sunday.

"Keider is on baby watch and that's great," Hinch said. "We don't really know exactly what day that's going to happen. We're trying to anticipate and prepare our guys to potentially cover the back side when Keider would pitch again. But I don't know quite yet how that's going to play out."

The off day Thursday gives him some room to maneuver the rotation. Montero's next start after Wednesday would be Monday in Toronto . By pushing the rotation back an extra day, Troy Melton , Drew Anderson and Valdez could start in the three games in Toronto Sept. 14-16.

As for Saturday's start, if Montero goes on the paternity list, the Tigers could recall lefty Andrew Sears from Toledo, even though he was optioned on Sept. 5.

None of that has been decided. What has been decided, though, is that the workloads of both Montero and Melton will be under scrutiny in these next two-plus weeks.

Montero went into his start Wednesday having thrown a career-high 143 innings and more than 2,000 pitches. Melton, who missed spring training and the first two months of the season with an elbow injury, is at 108 innings. He threw 54 big-league innings last season, including 8.1 in the postseason, plus 75 innings in the minors.

Hinch and pitching coach Chris Fetter are trying to balance health and safety with conditioning pitchers to run the full race. Which, as Hinch pointed out, isn't supposed to end in September.

"We're going to be careful," Hinch said. "But it's important for guys to go start to finish. We talk about workload right now and the nervousness that comes when pitchers get to uncharted territory. But we're only in early September. We're not even to the hard sprint to October which is when we want to play. You have to be really careful not to condition young players that now is the time to be guarded."

Hinch said with the off day Thursday, he can be a little more wary Montero, especially if he's going on paternity leave. And by leaving the Saturday start date open against Colorado , Melton will get two extra days, or more if Hinch wants to push him to the end of the Blue Jays series.

"I want to be very clear with them, the goal isn't just to finish at the end of September," he said. "We have to train for an extra month. October baseball is as intense as it gets."

The message is the same for position players.

"If Dillon (Dingler) is tired or Kevin (McGonigle) is beat up, yes, it happens in September," Hinch said. "But we want these guys preparing to play another 40 days, not another 15. That mentality has to be pushed on all of us."

articles.title: Why Jeff Hafley should keep it simple with these young Dolphins
articles.summary: What the NFL's youngest roster needs from Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS ― During the preseason, including joint practices, Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley was open about keeping schemes simple.

The key, Hafley explained, was getting a complete evaluation of the players.

It was not about tricking opponents with complex strategies.

It's my opinion that Hafley should take a similar approach in the regular season, starting with the season-opener at Las Vegas on Sunday, Sept. 13.

Keep it simple. Less complex. Limit risk.

Recently I asked Hafley about if he'll use his "gut" to potentially override some in-game recommendations from the analytics teams, such as punting or going for it on fourth down.

"I think you have a plan, and I think a lot of the times you try to stick with your plan, but there's always got to be the feel of the game and where it's going and the momentum of the game and how I think everything is going and what the team needs from me right now," Hafley said.

Much of the strategy will be determined the week before the game. Stick with the plan.

Miami is currently an underdog in 16 of 17 regular-season games. But the Dolphins have a shot on Sunday.

Photos of Miami Dolphins 53-man roster - until they add/drop players

Miami Dolphins roster is youngest in NFL

They're only 3.5-point underdogs and facing a beatable quarterback, Kirk Cousins .

If rookie Fernando Mendoza was making his first career start, it might make more sense to throw a few "kitchen sinks" at the youngster.

But Cousins has seen everything. There is no need to throw a bunch of blitzes at him that may confuse Miami's 14-member rookie class more than Cousins.

Keep it simple. Give the team a chance. Help limit busts from a very inexperienced secondary.

Blowouts can be demoralizing for a young group. Limiting blowouts could prove beneficial in the long-run.

Go for it on 4th-and-1 from Miami's 39-yard line on the first possession of the season?

We say punt. And that hurts to write. But punt.

Limit short fields for the defense. Limit tons of snaps for the defense. This team lacks depth.

Dolphins could play it conservative early on

Hafley noted he was among the leaders in going for it on fourth down at Boston College one season.

At times, BC was undermanned in a manner similar to what the Dolphins figure to face this year.

The goal this season is to, yes, try to win some games. But even more important is to evaluation of players, particularly young players.

Former Dolphins coach Dave Wannstedt, a mentor of Hafley's, used to say in so many words that the punt is not a bad play (certainly compared to a turnover on downs, interception or lost fumble).

Times have changed. Far more teams now are going for it on 4th-and-1.

But tapping into some of Wannstedt's mindset this season would not be the worst thing.

Could Miami roll out an exotic blitz here or later there this season?

Sure. But starting out "base" and "vanilla" seems the best way to go early in the season.

"I'm going to call what I believe our guys can execute at a high level," Hafley said, a few days before the opener.

Miami needs to evaluate their players in 1-on-1 situations this season. It's far less essential to scheme up free runners or 2-on-1's. Evaluation must be key to every decision.

Miami Dolphins ' Jeff Hafley could keep it vanilla early on

Miami has the youngest roster in the league. Keep it simple.

I once asked a college coach about how fast a young player was.

"That's great but if you're running the wrong way, you just get there faster," he said.

Miami figures to have some rookies running fast, but the wrong way on Sunday.

Keep it simple. Limit mistakes. Just play fast and free.

NFL preseason power rankings: Miami Dolphins start out near bottom

Joe Schad is a journalist covering the Miami Dolphins and the NFL at The Palm Beach Post . You can reach him at jschad@pbpost.com and follow him on Instagram and on X @schadjoe . Sign up for Joe's free weekly Dolphins Pulse Newsletter . Help support our work by subscribing today.

articles.title: Yankees news: 2 New York pitchers get crucial injury updates before playoffs
articles.summary: The New York Yankees received encouraging injury updates on Ryan Weathers and Fernando Cruz. Weathers has progressed to throwing from 75 feet while recoverin...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees received encouraging injury updates on Ryan Weathers and Fernando Cruz . Weathers has progressed to throwing from 75 feet while recovering from a left forearm flexor strain, while Cruz could soon resume throwing as he takes a non-surgical approach to a partially torn right UCL.

The updates provide New York with clearer recovery timelines as the club enters the final three weeks of the regular season at 82-62 and atop the AL wild-card standings. MLB.com's latest Yankees injury report outlined the next steps for both pitchers as they work toward potential returns.

"LHP Ryan Weathers Injury: Left forearm flexor strain IL date: Aug. 23 (15-day-IL) Expected return: Late September Status: Threw from 75 feet (40 throws) on Sept. 8, with plans to repeat process the next two days. Could begin throwing off a mound when he resumes after a day off on Sept. 11."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Cruz's timetable remains uncertain, while Weathers has already progressed further in his throwing program. MLB.com provided the following update on the right-hander:

"RHP Fernando Cruz Injury: Partially torn right ulnar collateral ligament IL date: Aug. 26 Expected return: TBD Status: Imaging performed on Aug. 26 revealed a partial tear of Cruz's right UCL. Met with Dr. Keith Meister, who advised a conservative approach for now. May resume throwing weekend of Sept. 11."

Weathers is further along in his recovery after throwing 40 times from 75 feet on Tuesday. He planned to repeat that work on Wednesday and Thursday before a scheduled day off, then he could progress to mound work.

The 26-year-old landed on the injured list after leaving his August 22 start against the Toronto Blue Jays . Imaging showed no structural damage. Before the injury, Weathers posted a 3.60 ERA with 143 strikeouts across 137 1/3 innings.

Cruz faces a less certain timetable with a partial tear in his right UCL. Dr. Keith Meister recommended a conservative approach, and he could resume throwing this weekend.

The 36-year-old has a 3.13 ERA and 67 strikeouts across 54 2/3 innings this season.

Both pitchers remain on the 15-day IL. Weathers has a late-September target, while Cruz has no established return date.

articles.title: Rutgers men's basketball coach Steve Pikiell reveals cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Rutgers coach Steve Pikiell said he plans to be still be involved with the team as he udnergoes chemotherapy.
articles.body:
Pikiell announced on Wednesday, Sept. 9 he was not feeling 100% a few months ago and visited the team doctors, and after undergoing testing, he learned he has cancer. He did not disclose what type of cancer it was.

"I am incredibly grateful to my team of doctors at RWJBarnabas Health and Memorial Sloan Kettering for guiding and supporting us through this difficult time," he said in a statement . "After a successful surgery, my doctors and I have a kick-ass game plan to finish treatment."

Pikiell still plans to be involved with the team "to the best of my ability" as he undergoes chemotherapy in the coming months, but associate head coach Brandin Knight will be at the helm when Pikiell is unable to.

Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn said there is no set timeline for when Pikiell will be able to fully return to the team.

"We are grateful to Coach Knight for his willingness to step up during this challenging time and to our entire staff for their great care and compassion for Coach and our student-athletes," Zinn said.

Pikiell arrived at Rutgers in 2016 and led the Scarlet Knights to the NCAA Tournament in 2021, their first apperance in 30 years, and winning its first tournament game in 38 years. Rutgers again made the tournament the following season.

In 10 seasons in Piscataway, Pikiell is 161–160.

Knight has been at Rutgers since Pikiell's arrival in 2016, elevating his way from assistant to associate coach.

Rutgers opens the 2026-27 season against New Haven on Nov. 6.

articles.body:
Celtic are on their travels again as they face St Johnstone at McDiarmid Park tonight (KO: 8pm).

And the Premiership match will see goalkeeper Sam Johnstone make his Celtic debut, as he comes in for Viljami Sinisalo , who is on the bench.

There's also a welcome return for Kasper Høgh up front, while Dane Murray slots into central defence in place of Cameron Carter-Vickers .

Kick-off in Perth is at 8pm and you can follow the build-up and all the action on the club website's Match Centre.

CELTIC: Johnstone, Donovan, Murray, Trusty, Scales, McGregor , Baur, Sørensen, Hassan, Høgh, Tounekti.Subs: Sinisalo, Lotomba , Nygren, Duran, Oxlade-Chamberlain, Mheuka, van den Berg, Forrest, Tierney

St. Johnstone Vs. Celtic - Wed, Sep 9th 2026, 19:00 Buy Tickets
